name: NE-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+27 partisan lean in a heavily Republican western Nebraska district
Incumbent Adrian Smith running with a large financial advantage ($1.8M raised vs $55K)
No outside spending against Smith and no general-election polling
model.rationale: The district's R+27 lean, Smith's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge leave Democratic challenger Becky Stille with no visible path; markets price her win chance at just 2%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting movement, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 21 points stands.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing Smith under 60% or a surge of outside spending against him would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Adrian Smith seeks another term in this western Nebraska district, one of the most Republican seats in the country at R+27. He has raised about $1.8 million and holds over $1 million on hand, while Democrat Becky Stille has raised roughly $55,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against Smith, and no independent or third-party candidates appear well funded.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Smith about a 97% chance of winning, consistent with the district's lean and the resource gap. The race is rated Safe Republican, with an expected margin of roughly 21 points.
